kinds.dependency: Installed through package-lock.json and redistributed with Ninerr when node_modules is shipped.
kinds.code-donor: Concepts or implementation patterns adapted into Ninerr-authored source; no donor files vendored.
kinds.guidance-donor: Studied for design guidance only; no donor code, text, or assets copied.
kinds.reference-only: Studied only; nothing copied and nothing may be copied.
kinds.optional-runtime: Invoked at runtime only if the user installed it; never shipped by Ninerr.
kinds.dev-tooling: Used to build or review Ninerr; not part of the product.
kinds.proprietary-authorized: Proprietary source the owner attests this project is authorized to use; raw source is kept out of the repository.
kinds.bundled-runtime: A pinned binary runtime fetched outside npm, verified by SHA-256 before it is unpacked, and redistributed with the desktop app.

entries.resolution: Category A. The founder's 2026-10-08 authorization (docs/provenance/FOUNDER_AUTHORIZATION_2026-10-08.md) gives official permission to copy, use, modify, adapt, combine, redistribute, rebrand, rename, refactor and incorporate the authorized source into Ninerr; it does not mention sublicensing, and nothing here claims it does. No Paper material remains to sublicense: no commit ever touched an imports/ path, N0-G4 replaced the recorded Paper MCP tool names with Ninerr's own catalog, and N0-G5 retired every Paper recovery record (docs/provenance/RETIRED_PAPER_RECORDS.md). What remains is behaviour compatibility implemented in Ninerr-authored code, so the Apache-2.0 grant covers only Ninerr's own work.

entries.evidence: The official release archives' LICENSE (sha256 5154e165bd6c2cc0cfbcd8916498c7abab0497923bafcd5cb07673fe8480087d in electron-v44.7.0-linux-x64.zip; Copyright (c) Electron contributors, Copyright (c) 2013-2020 GitHub Inc.). The archives are pinned by SHA-256 in scripts/desktop/electron.mjs, and the digests match both the release's SHASUMS256.txt and the electron@44.7.0 npm package's checksums.json. Ninerr's shell (packages/desktop) is project-owned.
entries.obligations: Redistributing the desktop app must carry Electron's LICENSE and LICENSES.chromium.html unchanged (both ship in the archive; for linux-x64 the latter lists 779 bundled components, sha256 3375e2a9bd7bc631738fde10be6548a76efe8cf5e4b8826b8140ba8b0c4d6353). They include LGPL-2.1 FFmpeg as the separately linked libffmpeg, whose source is Chromium's FFmpeg at the release's Chromium revision. Each packaged platform's LICENSES.chromium.html is classified at packaging (scripts/desktop/chromium-licenses.mjs): packaging fails if a component named under a non-permissive license has not been reviewed, and the reasons for each reviewed one are recorded there and in docs/evidence/PC9B_DESKTOP_PACKAGING_2026-10-08.md. Ninerr's copy of the MIT text is docs/provenance/ELECTRON_LICENSE.txt. The exact corresponding source of the runtime, for its LGPL components (Blink, statically linked; libffmpeg) and the rest, is bound in docs/provenance/ELECTRON_CORRESPONDING_SOURCE.json (Electron, Chromium and ffmpeg commits, verified live by scripts/desktop/corresponding-source.mjs --check); how a binary release offers it is a release-gate decision (docs/evidence/N0_G7B_ELECTRON_SOURCE_2026-10-09.md).
